children.name: Paragraph
children.characters:
I have always been interested in creating ideas and discovering problems.
During my undergraduate studies in Theatre, I moved toward dramaturgy because I wanted to understand how ideas are built, structured, and communicated — almost like being the architect of an idea.
After COVID, I decided to start an online business of my own. I needed a website, so I trusted someone to design it for me. A few months later, I discovered that they had, well... slightly exaggerated their web design skills.
So I started learning design myself.
What began as a necessity gradually became a serious interest in web design, UI/UX, and eventually product design.
My background in theatre and dramaturgy taught me to look beyond the obvious problem, understand different perspectives, and search for the story underneath the surface. Today, whenever I encounter a new problem, I get excited by one question:
“How many different ways can I solve this?”

children.name: Text
children.characters:
Joined the product team to redesign and improve the digital experience of a UK-based charity supporting migrant women and children through skills development, community support, and a platform to share their experiences.
Audited the existing website and design to identify opportunities for improving usability, information architecture, visual communication, and content clarity.
Leading the redesign of the digital product with a focus on clearly communicating who the organization serves, what it offers, and how users can engage with its services.
Translating the organization’s goals and the needs of its target audience into a clearer user-centered product experience and visual system.

children.name: Text
children.characters:
Collaborated with the founding team to transform a pet photography booking concept into a storytelling-driven web experience.
Defined the booking flow around the user's decision-making journey, balancing engagement, business needs, and customer trust.
Designed the end-to-end booking experience, combining on-site reservation steps with direct communication between the customer and the service provider.
Identified payment trust as a potential barrier to booking and designed a flow where payment was completed after the initial booking and direct confirmation with the customer.

children.name: Text
children.characters:
Co-founded and designed an industry-specific recruitment platform for the Health, Safety & Environment (HSE) industry, from initial concept to early-stage launch and validation.
Researched hiring challenges and user needs across job seekers and employers, translating insights into product requirements and user-centered solutions.
Designed the end-to-end recruitment journey, including job discovery, search, registration, job posting, and employer–candidate interactions.
Led end-to-end UX/UI design, including information architecture, user flows, wireframes, interaction design, and high-fidelity interfaces.
Validated the product organically with 100+ job seekers and employers during the early testing phase, using user feedback to identify usability and product improvements.
Contributed to organic user acquisition through community building, social media, and SEO-driven content, with blog content becoming a major source of website traffic and registrations from Google search.

children.name: Problem On the Windows 11 Lock Screen, users have limited access to features that don't necessarily require unlocking the device. The available features are also spread across different areas of the screen, which can make them harder to find and access, especially on larger displays. Goal Create a customizable Control Center that gives users access to more useful tools and notifications without repeatedly unlocking their device. The goal is to bring these features together in one place, similar to the quick-access experience users are familiar with on mobile devices.

Problem
On the Windows 11 Lock Screen, users have limited access to features that don't necessarily require unlocking the device.
The available features are also spread across different areas of the screen, which can make them harder to find and access, especially on larger displays.

Goal
Create a customizable Control Center that gives users access to more useful tools and notifications without repeatedly unlocking their device.
The goal is to bring these features together in one place, similar to the quick-access experience users are familiar with on mobile devices.

children.name: The current Lock Screen provides a few useful features, but they are distributed across different areas of the screen.

children.name: Based on the existing experience, several improvements could make the Lock Screen more useful and easier to access. 01 — Add more frequently used controls such as Volume, Bluetooth, Airplane Mode, and Power. 02 — Allow users to view app notifications directly from the Lock Screen. 03 — Move the media player to a more visible and accessible location. 04 — Give widgets a more suitable and organized space on the Lock Screen. 05 — Combine widgets, notifications, media, and quick settings into one dedicated panel. 06 — Allow users to choose which features appear in their Control Center through Windows Settings.

children.name: The final design brings notifications, widgets, media controls, and quick settings together in one unified Control Center. The interface is designed to provide quick access to the required features while keeping the information organized and easy to scan. It also introduces customization, allowing users to choose which features they want to see on their Lock Screen. The structure is designed with enough flexibility to support additional features in the future without changing the overall experience.

children.name: Since this project is a design concept and was not tested with real users, the evaluation phase was defined as a validation plan. The concept would be evaluated through usability testing to understand whether users can quickly find the information they need and access key features such as notifications, widgets, and quick settings from the lock screen. The evaluation would focus on task completion time, number of interactions, task success rate, and user satisfaction. We would also examine whether the notification grouping and information hierarchy are clear and intuitive. These findings would help determine whether the information hierarchy, notification structure, or quick-access controls need further refinement.

children.name: The core idea was to create a movie assistant that recommends films based on how the user wants to feel, rather than relying on traditional genres or familiar topics. To achieve this, I designed a system that uses AI to analyze movie data, along with audience and critic reviews, and map each film to different emotions and moods. This allows the system to understand not only what a movie is about, but also what kind of feeling it can create and when it might be suitable to watch. After watching a recommended film, users can provide feedback on how well it matched their selected mood. This feedback can be used to improve the AI's classification and gradually build a better understanding of each user's preferences.

children.name: Since the product was not implemented, the evaluation phase was planned rather than conducted. The system could be evaluated through both user feedback and behavioral data. After watching a recommended film, users would rate how well the movie matched the mood they had selected. We would also track how many recommendations users go through before choosing a movie and how often they change their selected mood. These signals would help identify where the recommendation experience needs improvement. For example, frequent mood changes or a high number of skipped recommendations could indicate that the mood classification or the ranking of movies within each mood needs to be refined. User feedback would provide an additional qualitative signal to validate whether the recommendations actually matched the intended feeling.

children.name: Details
children.characters: Age: 29 Background: Cinema - MA Role: Product Designer Based in: Tehran

children.name: Paragraph
children.characters:
I have always been interested in creating ideas and discovering problems.
During my undergraduate studies in Theatre, I moved toward dramaturgy because I wanted to understand how ideas are built, structured, and communicated — almost like being the architect of an idea.
After COVID, I decided to start an online business of my own. I needed a website, so I trusted someone to design it for me. A few months later, I discovered that they had, well... slightly exaggerated their web design skills.
So I started learning design myself.
What began as a necessity gradually became a serious interest in web design, UI/UX, and eventually product design.
My background in theatre and dramaturgy taught me to look beyond the obvious problem, understand different perspectives, and search for the story underneath the surface. Today, whenever I encounter a new problem, I get excited by one question:
“How many different ways can I solve this?”

Joined the product team to redesign and improve the digital experience of a UK-based charity supporting migrant women and children through skills development, community support, and a platform to share their experiences.
Audited the existing website and design to identify opportunities for improving usability, information architecture, visual communication, and content clarity.
Leading the redesign of the digital product with a focus on clearly communicating who the organization serves, what it offers, and how users can engage with its services.
Translating the organization’s goals and the needs of its target audience into a clearer user-centered product experience and visual system.

children.name: Text

Defined the booking flow around the user's decision-making journey, balancing engagement, business needs, and customer trust.
Designed the end-to-end booking experience, combining on-site reservation steps with direct communication between the customer and the service provider.
Identified payment trust as a potential barrier to booking and designed a flow where payment was completed after the initial booking and direct confirmation with the customer.

Contributed to organic user acquisition through community building, social media, and SEO-driven content, with blog content becoming a major source of website traffic and registrations from Google search.

children.name: Problem On the Windows 11 Lock Screen, users have limited access to features that don't necessarily require unlocking the device. The available features are also spread across different areas of the screen, which can make them harder to find and access, especially on larger displays. Goal Create a customizable Control Center that gives users access to more useful tools and notifications without repeatedly unlocking their device. The goal is to bring these features together in one place, similar to the quick-access experience users are familiar with on mobile devices.

Problem
On the Windows 11 Lock Screen, users have limited access to features that don't necessarily require unlocking the device.
The available features are also spread across different areas of the screen, which can make them harder to find and access, especially on larger displays.

Goal
Create a customizable Control Center that gives users access to more useful tools and notifications without repeatedly unlocking their device.
The goal is to bring these features together in one place, similar to the quick-access experience users are familiar with on mobile devices.

children.name: The current Lock Screen provides a few useful features, but they are distributed across different areas of the screen.

children.name: Based on the existing experience, several improvements could make the Lock Screen more useful and easier to access. 01 — Add more frequently used controls such as Volume, Bluetooth, Airplane Mode, and Power. 02 — Allow users to view app notifications directly from the Lock Screen. 03 — Move the media player to a more visible and accessible location. 04 — Give widgets a more suitable and organized space on the Lock Screen. 05 — Combine widgets, notifications, media, and quick settings into one dedicated panel. 06 — Allow users to choose which features appear in their Control Center through Windows Settings.

We would also examine whether the notification grouping and information hierarchy are clear and intuitive. These findings would help determine whether the information hierarchy, notification structure, or quick-access controls need further refinement.

children.name: When people want to watch a movie together, choosing what to watch can take a significant amount of time. They often have several options, but still don't know which movie fits their mood at that moment. They need to check genres, ratings, reviews, and story summaries to understand whether a movie is right for them. This becomes more frustrating when several people are involved, because everyone may have a different preference. As a result, a large part of their limited leisure time can be spent looking for a movie instead of watching one.

children.name: The core idea was to create a movie assistant that recommends films based on how the user wants to feel, rather than relying on traditional genres or familiar topics. To achieve this, I designed a system that uses AI to analyze movie data, along with audience and critic reviews, and map each film to different emotions and moods. This allows the system to understand not only what a movie is about, but also what kind of feeling it can create and when it might be suitable to watch. After watching a recommended film, users can provide feedback on how well it matched their selected mood. This feedback can be used to improve the AI's classification and gradually build a better understanding of each user's preferences.

children.name: Since the product was not implemented, the evaluation phase was planned rather than conducted. The system could be evaluated through both user feedback and behavioral data. After watching a recommended film, users would rate how well the movie matched the mood they had selected. We would also track how many recommendations users go through before choosing a movie and how often they change their selected mood. These signals would help identify where the recommendation experience needs improvement. For example, frequent mood changes or a high number of skipped recommendations could indicate that the mood classification or the ranking of movies within each mood needs to be refined. User feedback would provide an additional qualitative signal to validate whether the recommendations actually matched the intended feeling.

For the Gadget Grid project, a technology news website, the goal was to blend classic design aesthetics with a modern visual style without overdoing either approach.
The design was primarily inspired by the work of Dieter Rams. Sharp edges and angular elements were combined with rounded corners, while an aluminum-like texture was applied to the background to evoke the feel of modern gadgets and consumer electronics.

children.name: Text
children.characters:
To bring more character to the interface, high-contrast accent colors were used alongside the broken and geometric frame shapes, creating a subtle sense of nostalgia.
As this is a news website, the focus was on creating a distinctive yet simple design, allowing users to access and consume content with ease.
